name: Question 8
problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0 \\ 7{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}}{5} \\  & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2(0)}{5} \\  & =-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Question 8

Find an eigenvector of A=[21−20−31004] that corresponds to the eigenvalue λ=−3.

a
 [7−10]
b
 [−170]
c
 [−510]
d
[−150]
e
 [5−10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=−3. So, we obtain

A−λI=[21−20−31004]−(−3)[100010001]=[51−2001007].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{5x1+x2−2x3=0x3=07x3=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[51−2000100070]R3:=R3+(−7)R2∼[51−2000100000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 1st and the 3rd). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x3=0. Substituting this into the first equation, we get x1=−x2+2x35=−x2+2(0)5=−x25. Therefore, the general solution is [−x25x20],x2∈R.

Setting, for instance, x2=5, we get the eigenvector v=[−150].
